title: Renewables Power the Orbit? Achieving Sustainable Space Edge Computing via QoS-Aware Offloading.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are becoming integral to 6G infrastructure, but increasing in-orbit computation accelerates battery degradation and raises sustainability concerns. Meanwhile, renewable-heavy regions worldwide experience persistent energy curtailment due to transmission bottlenecks, leaving substantial clean energy stranded near generation sites. We identify a satellite-grid co-design opportunity: adaptively offloading task-critical data from satellite to data centers co-located with renewable power plants. However, realizing this vision requires jointly considering intermittent and capacity-limited communication windows, as well as time-varying electricity budgets. In this paper, we propose SQSO, a Sustainable and QoS-aware Satellite Offloading framework that models per-interval task offloading as a constrained optimization over dynamic topology and electricity prices. Under this framework, we design $\text{AO}^2$, an adaptive offloading orchestration algorithm to solve the formulated optimization problem. Using Starlink-scale simulations and real-world electricity price traces, $\text{AO}^2$ reduces energy consumption by up to 76.03% and battery life consumption by up to 76.85% compared to state-of-the-art schemes, while also lowering task delay. This work highlights that sustainable scaling of LEO constellations requires co-design of space networking and renewable energy infrastructure, while our solution promotes renewable-aware task offloading and cross-domain collaboration for space-energy integration in the 6G era.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: NeuroForensics: Unmasking Covert Backdoor Attack via Endogenous Defense.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates decentralized training without exchanging raw data, yet remains inherently susceptible to backdoor attacks. Existing defenses predominantly rely on statistical outlier detection, assumed that malicious updates exhibit significant deviations from benign ones. However, this premise is fundamentally flawed in real-world scenarios, particularly against covert backdoor attacks within non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data conditions. In this paper, we propose a robust FL defense framework, called NeuroForensics, that employs a target-oriented approach to resist covert backdoor attacks under Non-IID data characteristics. To uncover endogenous anomalies, we project high-dimensional model weights into a Posterior Probability Matrix via Pseudo Feature Vectors (PFV). This projection helps magnify the endogenous divergences between malicious and benign clients. Furthermore, to characterize these disparities across multiple dimensions, we incorporate a multi-metric fusion strategy that synthesizes matrix features into a unified anomaly detection score, enabling an adaptive thresholding mechanism to accurately isolate malicious clients. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that NeuroForensics significantly outperforms existing defense schemes, suppressing backdoor success rates while preserving high main-task utility, even under covert attacks and extreme Non-IID conditions.

title: Toward Communication-Sensing Integrated Cloud-Network Monitoring: Real-Time Vibration Event Recognition on Underground Optical Cables.
abstract: Underground optical cables are key assets in cloudnetwork infrastructure, and distributed optical fiber sensing enables them to serve as both communication media and sensing resources for external disturbance monitoring. This paper presents a real-time vibration event recognition framework for communication-sensing integrated underground opticalcable monitoring based on $\Phi$-OTDR signals. To avoid temporal information leakage, continuous vibration traces are divided into non-overlapping training, validation, and testing periods before sliding-window segmentation and Z-score standardization. The proposed SE-DMRCB model integrates parallel multiscale 1D convolutions, stacked residual blocks, and squeezeand-excitation attention to capture both impulsive and periodic vibration patterns. Bayesian optimization is employed to select key hyperparameters for balancing recognition accuracy and model complexity. Experiments on a real-world underground optical-cable deployment with eight vibration-event categories show that the proposed method achieves 99.84% test accuracy with an end-to-end recognition latency of 10.55 ms per window, which is much lower than the 512 ms window-update interval. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can support online recognition and sensing-assisted diagnosis for cloud-network infrastructure operation.

title: Temporal Predictive Joint Hybrid Beamforming Framework for Mitigating Channel Aging in High-Mobility MIMO-OFDM Systems.
abstract: As a key technology for enhancing spectral efficiency, Frequency Division Duplexing (FDD) massive multipleinput multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) is limited by channel aging in high-mobility scenarios. The latency in channel estimation and feedback renders Base Station (BS) CSI outdated relative to rapid channel variations caused by Doppler shifts, leading to beam misalignment. To combat the issue, we propose a unified framework called Predictive Attention-aided Multi-Scale Hybrid Beamforming (PAMS-HBF). The architecture integrates a Learnable Pilot Sensing (LPS) module for adaptive downlink pilot design, functioning for both downlink pilot transmission and user-side pilot sensing, alongside a Long Short-Term Channel Prediction (LSTCP) module using LSTM to forecast CSI for aging compensation. A Multi-Scale CSI Feedback (MCF) module employs multi-scale convolutions to capture diverse features for compression. An Efficient Channel Attention Beamforming (ECAB) module at the BS reconstructs features to generate beamforming matrices. Experimental results demonstrate that PAMS-HBF maintains consistent performance across different velocities. Comparisons show its superiority over traditional algorithms and static deep learning schemes. The proposed method at sufficient feedback bits exceeds the lossless feedback baseline by approximately 23.1%.

title: Tremerity-Fi: Non-Contact Daily-Life Tremor Severity Assessment by Commercial mmWave Radar.
abstract: Tremor is a common symptom of neurological diseases. The regular assessment of daily tremors facilitates the evaluation of disease progression and assists clinicians in optimizing treatment strategies. However, current home monitoring solutions have difficulty in dealing with user cooperation, privacy concerns, environmental interference, and system generalization, leading to feasibility concerns in activities of daily living (ADL). To this end, we propose Tremerity-Fi, a non-contact and privacy-friendly tremor severity assessment system based on mmWave radar. To realize Tremerity-Fi, we first design an adaptive beamforming algorithm to accurately identify useful but weak signals from numerous reflections captured in the environment. Second, unlike primary reflections commonly used in mmWave sensing, we leverage multipath reflections that carry useful information about the target's motion, even though they are generally considered harmful, to help reconstruct hand signals and improve sensing performance. Furthermore, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation algorithm to improve the ability to adapt to unseen environments and users. We collect a diverse dataset of 5 patients and 25 healthy subjects in 3 scenarios, such as offices, homes, and hospitals. Extensive experiments show that our system achieves 94.51% accuracy in tremor detection, about 5 higher than the SOTA mmWave radar method, and 89.13% in tremor severity assessment, demonstrating its sufficient potential as a tremor monitoring assistant for patients with neurological diseases.

title: Joint Optimization of Video Recommendation and Cooperative Edge Caching for Maximizing Profit.
abstract: The rapid growth of multi-version video-on-demand (VoD) services places increasing pressure on mobile networks. Edge caching offers a promising solution by bringing content closer to mobile users (MUs). However, practical edge caching systems face a fundamental challenge: MUs exhibit highly varied preferences across video contents and bitrates, whereas edge resources are limited, costly, and influenced by pricing decisions from mobile network operators (MNOs). In this paper, we study a novel, profit-oriented joint optimization problem that integrates personalized video recommendation, cooperative multi-version edge caching, soft cache hits, and economic incentives. We model the interaction between the MNO and the video provider (VP) as a Stackelberg game, which explicitly captures the coupling between pricing decisions, caching strategies, and various demands of MUs. We also show that the studied problem is NP-hard due to its non-convex structure and the presence of mixed discrete-continuous decision variables. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Backward-Induction Stackelberg framework, in which the MNO optimizes cache-leasing prices via an iterative distance-weighted strategy, while the VP solves its NP-hard joint decision problem through block coordinate descent combined with relaxation-and-rounding techniques. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art schemes, improving the MNO’s revenue by up to 32.18% and the VP’s revenue by up to 33.43%, while remaining robust under diverse system configurations.

title: CF-BAD: Coarse-to-Fine Granularity BGP Anomaly Detection for Prefix Hijacking.
abstract: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) serves as the defacto standard for inter-domain routing, yet it fundamentally lacks authentication and validation mechanisms, leaving the global Internet infrastructure vulnerable to both malicious attacks and inadvertent misconfigurations. Traditional detection approaches often fall short in accurately identifying prefix hijacking, particularly in small-scale events, and typically produce results that are difficult to interpret. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CF-BAD, a novel anomaly detection framework. Specifically, to capture the subtle patterns characteristic of small-scale anomalies, we construct a dual-granular feature tensor that integrates both time- and frequency-domain information derived from raw BGP data. We further introduce an adaptive mask mechanism tailored for the Swin-Transformer architecture, enabling enhanced representation learning across both coarse- and fine-grained knowledge. Our detection model also incorporates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) unit to effectively capture long- and short-term temporal dependencies. To improve interpretability, we devise a novel layer-wise root cause analysis (RCA) method that provides explainable insights via hierarchical decomposition. Extensive experiments conducted on 15 real-world anomaly events comprising 343 million BGP messages in total demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in both detection and RCA accuracy across the majority of cases.

title: The Imitation Game: Using Large Language Models to Disrupt Chinese Chat-Based Cybercrime.
abstract: Chat-based cybercrime has emerged as a pervasive threat, with attackers leveraging real-time messaging platforms to conduct scams that rely on trust-building, deception, and psychological manipulation. Traditional defense mechanisms, which operate on static rules or shallow content filters, struggle to identify these conversational threats, especially when attackers use multimedia obfuscation and context-aware dialogue. In this work, we ask a provocative question inspired by the classic Imitation Game: Can machines convincingly pose as human victims to turn deception against cybercriminals? We present LURE (LLM-based User Response Engagement), the first system to deploy Large Language Models (LLMs) as active agents (not as passive classifiers) embedded within adversarial chat environments. LURE combines automated discovery, adversarial interaction, and OCR-based analysis of image-embedded payment data. Applied to the setting of Chinese illicit video chat scams on Telegram, our system engaged 53 actors across 98 groups. In over 56% of interactions, the LLM maintained multi-round conversations without being noticed as a bot, effectively “winning” the imitation game. Our findings reveal key behavioral patterns in scam operations, such as payment flows, upselling strategies, and platform migration tactics.
